findings.title: Unsubscribe can 500 on a missing TopicUser and bypasses notification bookkeeping
findings.body: The new action does `tu = TopicUser.find_by(...)` and then calls `tu.notification_level` and `tu.save!` without a nil check. A logged-in user who can see the topic but has no TopicUser row (for example a forwarded email link, or a record removed by cleanup) will get a 500 instead of being unsubscribed. Even when the row exists, assigning and saving it directly bypasses TopicUser.change, so notifications_changed_at/notifications_reason_id are not updated and no MessageBus notification_level_change is published; other open tabs keep the old notification state. Use TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: target_level), which creates the row and publishes the change.

findings.title: Per-topic unsubscribe is a CSRF-able GET with no token
findings.body: The new `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` / `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"` routes perform a state change (notification_level) and rely only on the session cookie. topics_controller skips check_xhr for this action, so non-XHR requests are accepted, and the JSON form `/t/123/unsubscribe.json` bypasses the slug check because `params[:slug].blank?` is only rejected for non-JSON requests. A malicious page can therefore include `` (or many IDs) and silently mute a logged-in victim from topics. Make this a POST with CSRF protection or use a signed per-email token; do not mutate state on an unauthenticated GET.

findings.title: Unsubscribe is not idempotent; reloading the link mutes further
findings.body: The action always computes a new level from the current one: watching/tracking goes to regular, then regular goes to muted. Because the unsubscribe URL is a GET, refreshing the confirmation page or opening the same email link again invokes the action again and keeps lowering the level. A user who unsubscribed once from a watched topic and reloads to read the confirmation will be muted. Set a fixed target level (or no-op when the current level is already at/below it) so the operation is idempotent.

findings.title: Global unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url from every caller
findings.body: The shared `unsubscribe_link` translation now unconditionally interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Email::MessageBuilder calls `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` for every email with `add_unsubscribe_link: true`, but this PR only supplies the new key in UserNotifications#send_notification_email. Any other mailer or plugin using MessageBuilder with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument at send time. Either keep the existing preferences-only fallback or update all callers/make the per-topic sentence conditional.

findings.title: No test asserts the new per-topic unsubscribe link or controller behavior
findings.body: The spec change only adds `unsubscribe_url` to the builder so the existing translation does not fail; the assertions still check only the user-preferences URL and the List-Unsubscribe header, never the new per-topic link. There is also no controller/request spec for TopicsController#unsubscribe covering a missing TopicUser, notification-level transitions, the slug redirect, or the JSON/CSRF path. Add assertions for the rendered link and controller specs for those branches.
